source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the pinned family names, maternal identification, brothers and sisters, and rejection.
key_decisions.before: Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
key_decisions.after: Isn’t this the carpenter, Mary’s son, and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves could not rather than silently changing it to would not; keeps the exception.
key_decisions.before: He could do no work of power there except to lay his hands on a few sick people and heal them.
key_decisions.after: He could do no miracle there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he could do no deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains Mark’s allowance of a staff and all three prohibitions without harmonizing another Gospel.
key_decisions.before: He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—
key_decisions.after: He told them to take nothing for the journey except a staff—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: He charged them to take nothing for the journey except a staff; no bread, no bag, no money in their belts;

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves permission for sandals and the source’s shift into direct address about tunics.
key_decisions.before: but to wear sandals and not put on two tunics.
key_decisions.after: They were to wear sandals. “But do not wear two tunics,” he said.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: but to wear sandals and not to put on two tunics.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps rejection, departure, and testimony without adding a Sodom saying absent from this source.
key_decisions.before: If any place will not welcome you or listen to you, leave and shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them.”
key_decisions.after: If any place will not welcome you and its people will not listen to you, leave it and shake the dust off your feet as a testimony to them.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And if any place will not welcome you and they refuse to hear you, as you leave, shake off the dust that is on your feet as a testimony against them.”

key_decisions.rationale: Follows plural people were saying and preserves the reported causal explanation rather than attributing it immediately to Herod.
key_decisions.before: King Herod heard about Jesus, because his name had become well known. Some were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him.”
key_decisions.after: King Herod heard about Jesus, whose name had become well known. People were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead. That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: King Herod heard of it, for his name had become known. Some were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and for this reason these powers are at work in him.”

key_decisions.rationale: Follows pinned puzzled, not did many things, and preserves Herod’s conflicted response and protection.
key_decisions.before: because Herod feared John, knowing he was a righteous and holy man, and protected him. When Herod listened to him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he still liked to listen.
key_decisions.after: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. When he listened to John, he was deeply puzzled, yet he liked hearing him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. And when he heard him, he was greatly perplexed; and yet he heard him gladly.

key_decisions.rationale: Follows autēs tēs Hērōdiados as Herodias’s own daughter and does not import the alternative daughter-name reading.
key_decisions.before: Herodias’s own daughter came in and danced, and she pleased Herod and his guests. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
key_decisions.after: Herodias’s own daughter came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And when his daughter Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests; and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it.”

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the contrary wind, ancient time designation, walking on the sea, and unexplained intention to pass by.
key_decisions.before: He saw them struggling at the oars because the wind was against them. Around the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them walking on the sea, and he intended to pass by them.
key_decisions.after: He saw them struggling at the oars, because the wind was against them. Around the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And seeing that they were distressed in rowing, for the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night he came toward them, walking on the sea; and he intended to pass by them.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains all as the scope of seeing, immediate reassurance, and the self-identification without adding a title.
key_decisions.before: because they all saw him and were terrified. Immediately he spoke to them: “Take courage. I am. Do not be afraid.”
key_decisions.after: because they all saw him and were terrified. At once he spoke to them: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke with them and said, “Take courage; I am. Do not be afraid.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the explanatory link to the feeding and the hard-heart image rather than a psychological paraphrase.
key_decisions.before: because they had not understood about the loaves; instead, their hearts were hardened.
key_decisions.after: for they had not understood about the loaves; their hearts were hardened.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: for they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves all three settings, public places, the garment fringe, and the full scope of healing.
key_decisions.before: Wherever he entered—villages, cities, or the countryside—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his cloak. Everyone who touched it was made well.
key_decisions.after: Wherever he went—villages, towns, or farms—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his cloak. Everyone who touched him was healed.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And wherever he entered villages, or cities, or countryside, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.
